title: [CQ-M07u] Test rows for two QA-found mutant survivors: vm-control's default runner probe, certification report equality
description:
Slice of CQ-M07 (task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8, the final acceptance row). Filed by its planner architect-c33f294e on 2026-11-04. It collects two QA hand-forwards posted on that row. Both are test gaps, not defects: the shipped code is correct, but a regression would go unseen. This row is tests only.

1. vm-control's production runner probe (comment-1834b0bb, QA qa-1b5727b1 on CQ-M07g task-9076afab)
- In scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs, every VC-C3/VC-R2 row injects runnerAlive. So three mutants pass every test: M28 (cleanupReport `runnerAlive = runnerProbe` changed to `() => false`), M29 (the same in reconcileReport) and M30 (runVmControl `deps.runnerAlive ?? (() => false)`).
- Any of them would purge a seat VM whose runner is still alive on this host.
- The row to add, in scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs:
  - one seat record whose runner is this test process (`${process.pid}@<token>` in the format the production probe parses), with host localRunnerHost() and platform process.platform;
  - the fake daemon says the seat is gone, and the lease is free;
  - call cleanupReport, reconcileReport and runVmControl (deps.call only) with NO runnerAlive;
  - expect the record preserved (or held) with reason 'runner-alive' and zero provider delete calls.

2. certification report equality (comment-66f37d9b, QA qa-97c4310b on CQ-M07a task-5a635bc9)
- In packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/certificationEvidence.test.ts, 6 strict-to-loose swaps (=== to ==) survive in the checkCertificationReport port: report.kind, version, transport, provider.name, executionReady and the check-row id.
- Add refused VARIANTS rows with JSON type-confusion values: version '1' and true; kind ['isolation-certification']; transport ['injected'] with certified false; provider name ['multipass']; executionReady 0; one check id ['provision'].
- Each must be refused with the reader's existing fixed code.

DELIVERABLE: new rows in those two test files only.

NOT IN SCOPE: any runtime change (vm-control.mjs, certificationEvidence.ts, certify.mjs); other test files; docs.

VERIFICATION: `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs`, then, in a git-archive snapshot of HEAD with this task's test file overlaid (npm ci there, env -i with Linux node 24), `npx vitest run src/delivery/certificationEvidence.test.ts`.
definitionOfDone: local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs has the default-probe row: a seat record whose runner is this process on this host, the daemon saying gone and the lease free, cleanupReport, reconcileReport and runVmControl run with no injected runnerAlive. Each keeps the record with reason 'runner-alive' and makes zero provider delete calls.
Mutants M28, M29 and M30 (comment-1834b0bb) each fail that row. The completion summary gives the scratch-copy evidence.

certificationEvidence.test.ts has refused rows for the type-confusion values in comment-66f37d9b, each expecting the reader's existing fixed code. An === to == mutant of each of the 6 compared fields fails its row. The completion summary gives the scratch-copy evidence.
`node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs` passes, and `npx vitest run src/delivery/certificationEvidence.test.ts` passes in a git-archive snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
Type-confusion rows in packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/certificationEvidence.test.ts (DoD 3). Edit tool in W. Make two insertions, exactly as in the reference diff /mnt/d/moe-scratch/d3a9-win/intended.diff.

(a) Insert directly after the line `for (const { platform, arch, versionSuffix: v } of CERTIFICATION_PINS.hosts) VARIANTS.push(...)`, the line before `describe('drift', () => {`:
```ts
// JSON type confusion: each value is == (never ===) to what its field accepts, so an === to == swap of that one comparison accepts it.
const CONFUSED: Array<[string, 'SCHEMA' | 'CHECKS', Report]> = [
  ['(t1) version as the string 1', 'SCHEMA', valid({ version: '1' })], ['(t2) version true', 'SCHEMA', valid({ version: true })],
  ['(t3) kind as a one-item array', 'SCHEMA', valid({ kind: ['isolation-certification'] })], ['(t4) executionReady 0', 'SCHEMA', valid({ executionReady: 0 })],
  ['(t5) transport injected as a one-item array', 'SCHEMA', { ...injected, transport: ['injected'] }],
  ['(t6) transport native as a one-item array', 'SCHEMA', valid({ transport: ['native'], certified: false })],
  ['(t7) provider name as a one-item array', 'SCHEMA', valid({ provider: { name: ['multipass'], version: null } })],
  ['(t8) a check id as a one-item array', 'CHECKS', valid({ checks: edit(passing(), 0, { id: ['provision'] }) })],
];
for (const [name, , value] of CONFUSED) VARIANTS.push([name, value, false]);
```
(b) Inside describe('drift'), directly after the `it.each(VARIANTS)('%s: the port and validateCertificationReport agree', ...)` block, insert:
```ts
  it.each(CONFUSED)('%s is refused as CERTIFICATION_REPORT_%s', (_name, code, value) => {
    expect(checkCertificationReport(value)).toStrictEqual({ ok: false, code: `CERTIFICATION_REPORT_${code}` });
  });
```
Why:
- Each value is == but not === to what its field accepts: a one-item array's string form, true == 1, '1' == 1, 0 == false. So an === to == swap of exactly that comparison accepts it.
- Pushed into VARIANTS as a refused row, each value also goes through the drift row, so certify.mjs validateCertificationReport must refuse it too. It does: it uses === and ['native','injected'].includes.
- The second it.each pins the reader's existing fixed code: CERTIFICATION_REPORT_SCHEMA for the six report-level values, CERTIFICATION_REPORT_CHECKS for the check id (validChecks rejects the row).
- transport gets two rows because it has two killable swaps: (t5) for `transport === 'injected'` and (t6) for `transport === 'native' ||`. A third swap, inside `certified === (transport === 'native' && ...)`, is an equivalent mutant: a transport that passes the earlier strict test is a string, where == and === agree. Name it as equivalent in the summary, with no row for it.
- The (tN) prefixes let checkRefs[2] pin which row died, because vitest prints `> (tN) ` on a FAIL line.
- Keep two rows per line where they fit, within the file's existing width of about 180 characters (comment-66f37d9b's advice).

Plan-time results:
- 99/99 pass (83 at base, plus 8 VARIANTS rows and 8 code rows).
- tsc with a scratch tsconfig (types node, vitest/globals) on this file: 0 errors, the same as the base.
- Each of the 7 swaps fails only its own rows: 4 for version, 2 for every other field.

Verification, once, after steps 1-2 (DoD 2-5), from W's root. Run each checkRef in its own Bash call, because each one cds into its own snapshot. checkRefs[0] is the gate: its fresh exit code and output are the moe.complete_task verification. checkRefs[1] and checkRefs[2] give the mutant evidence for the summary.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Assert the fixed code inside the VARIANTS it.each. Rejected: its tuple is [name, value, accepted], so every existing row would need a code. A separate CONFUSED table pushed into VARIANTS keeps the drift agreement and adds the fixed code for exactly the new rows.
- One transport row, as comment-66f37d9b suggests. Not enough: `transport === 'native' ||` is a second killable swap that the ['injected'] row does not kill, so (t6) covers it. The swap inside `certified === (transport === 'native' && ...)` is an equivalent mutant.
- Testing runnerProbe directly. VC-P1 already does, and it cannot see M28-M30, which are the defaults in the report functions and runVmControl.
- A separate live process as the runner. Unnecessary: this test process is alive by construction, and the probe only sends signal 0.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- node --test uses the spec reporter here: a failing test prints `✖ <name>`, and the summary prints `ℹ fail N`.
- vitest prints a FAIL line as `> drift > <title>`, so the (tN) prefixes pin the row.
- The shared checkout's packages/moe-daemon/node_modules are Windows-native. npm ci in a /tmp snapshot takes about 2 s with node v24.21.0.
- certificationEvidence.test.ts imports scripts/local-runner/{certify.mjs,certified-provider.json,guest-supervisor.py}, so its snapshot needs scripts/.
- Test files are not type-checked by the build. A scratch tsconfig (`types: [node, vitest/globals]`) showed 0 errors, before and after.
planningNotes.risks:
- If HEAD moves before the claim and a mutant anchor changes, the replacer exits 9 and checkRefs[1] or [2] fails loudly. Run that mutant by hand against the moved expression and say so in the summary; never weaken the check.
- QA re-running checkRefs[0] in the control checkout runs node --test in place, which is fine, and copies the landed test file, which is a no-op.
- The certification file's lines run to about 180 chars; keep the new ones within that.
- The CQ-M07 final row (task-1a8f1d0e) already depends on this task and declares neither file, so no ordering change is needed.
